item.title: The Royal Society
item.description: The Royal Society Summary The Royal Society of London for Improving Natural Knowledge, incorporated by Royal Charter in 1662, was the first permanent institution devoted to experimental natural philosophy in the English-speaking world.

item.title: Social Orders and Ranks in 1688
item.description: Social Orders and Ranks in 1688 Summary Gregory King, Lancaster Herald of Arms, included in his Natural and Political Observations upon the State and Condition of England (1696) a celebrated classification of the English population by social degree.

item.title: Sir Cloudesley Shovel
item.description: Sir Cloudesley Shovel Summary Sir Cloudesley Shovel (1650–1707) was one of the most respected English admirals of the late 17th and early 18th centuries, whose career spanned from the Third Dutch War through the War of the Spanish Succession.

item.title: East India Company
item.description: East India Company The Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies, chartered by Queen Elizabeth on 31 December 1600, was by the late 17th century the most powerful chartered trading company in England.

item.title: Admiral John Benbow
item.description: Admiral John Benbow Summary Admiral John Benbow (1653–1702) was an English naval commander whose career rose from a merchant seaman to vice-admiral of the blue.

item.title: Battle of Naseby
item.description: Battle of Naseby (14 June 1645) Summary The Battle of Naseby, fought on 14 June 1645 in the rolling fields of Northamptonshire, was the decisive engagement of the First English Civil War.
